records.verificationNote: Common Formulary pp.50-52 lists SSRI products with '#', which the legend on p.7 defines as carved out and billed to fee-for-service Medicaid. SSRIs do not appear on the Single PDL text (only olanzapine/fluoxetine in the antipsychotic-antidepressant combination class). Because the SSRI rows are carved out, coverage is through FFS, not the MHP. The carve-out list itself is a separate MDHHS link not in this document. Sig is standard label dosing. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: Carve-out confirmed (CF legend p.7, definition p.2), but fee-for-service coverage terms (PA, quantity or age limits) live in the MPPL, which was not retrieved; lowered to partial. records.verificationNote: Fetched the cited PDF (WebFetch's built-in extraction returned only binary/metadata on this 80-page/3.7MB file, consistent with this repo's known large-PDF extraction gap -- the saved binary was re-read locally via the PDF-tools MCP's page-range and search functions instead). Page 1 confirms the document title '2026 Prescription Drug List, Effective: January 1, 2026, UnitedHealthcare & affiliated companies' -- used as effectiveDate and matches the payer/PBM (OptumRx, named explicitly on page 6 under 'How to obtain prior authorization': 'optumrx.com' and 'Optum Rx prior authorization team'). Pages 4-6 confirm the 3-tier legend (Tier 1 lowest cost / Tier 2 mid-range / Tier 3 highest cost) and the symbol legend: E = 'May be excluded from coverage or subject to Prior Authorization in Connecticut, New Jersey and New York', PA = prior authorization required, QL = quantity limit, ST = step therapy, SP = specialty. The Antidepressants -- Drugs for Depression section (PDF pages 12-13) was located via a direct text search for 'Antidepressants' rather than reading the whole 80-page document, then read in full. All six oral SSRI molecules were confirmed verbatim: citalopram hydrobromide oral tablet (Tier 1, no code), CELEXA brand (marked E), escitalopram oxalate oral tablet (Tier 1) and oral solution 5mg/5ml (Tier 2), LEXAPRO brand (marked E), fluoxetine HCl oral capsule and oral solution (Tier 1, no code), fluoxetine HCl oral tablet 10mg (Tier 3, QL) and 20mg/60mg (Tier 3), PROZAC brand (marked E), fluvoxamine maleate immediate-release (Tier 1) and ER (Tier 3, QL), paroxetine HCl oral tablet (Tier 1) and ER (Tier 3, QL), PAXIL and PAXIL CR brands (marked E, PAXIL CR also QL), sertraline HCl oral tablet and oral concentrate (Tier 1, no code) but a separately-listed 'sertraline hcl oral capsule' line marked E and QL, and ZOLOFT brand (marked E). Sertraline tablet was selected as the representative preferred agent because it is the most broadly first-line-prescribed generic SSRI in clinical practice and reads cleanest (Tier 1, no code) among the six Tier-1 no-restriction options -- this single-agent selection among clinically-tied, equally-covered options is an inference, consistent with the convention used across every other payer in this dataset's ssri-oral class. The 50 mg strength and once-daily sig are standard prescribing convention, not stated in the PDL itself (which lists drug name, tier, and restriction codes only, no dosing guidance). No class-wide step-therapy or PA criterion appears anywhere in the Antidepressants section that applies across all SSRI molecules as a group (the ST codes present in this section attach only to non-SSRI agents: AUVELITY, FETZIMA, TRINTELLIX, VIIBRYD). The anomalous 'sertraline hcl oral capsule' E/QL line item is flagged rather than silently omitted or merged into the clean tablet/concentrate entries, since it carries a distinct restriction code the tablet/concentrate forms do not. [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]

records.verificationNote: Read directly from the 'Humana Premier Rx Plan (PDP) Formulary 26402' 2026 Prescription Drug Guide (Y0040_PDG26_FINAL_5C_C 20260005PDG2640226C_v15), cover page states 'Updated 08/01/2026'. The Antidepressants section spans pages 22-23 of the PDF (labeled '2026 HUMANA FORMULARY UPDATED 08/01/2026'), which lists all six named SSRI generics (citalopram, escitalopram oxalate, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine hcl, sertraline) with exact tier numbers and utilization-management codes (MO/QL only -- no PA or ST flags on any dosage form of any of the six generics). Confirmed: sertraline tablet (25/50/100 mg), citalopram tablet, escitalopram tablet, and fluoxetine capsule are all Tier 1 - Preferred Generic (definition read from page 5: 'Generic or brand drugs that are available at the lowest cost share for the plan'); paroxetine tablet and fluvoxamine tablet are Tier 2 - Generic; less-common dosage forms (solutions, ER tablets, capsules of escitalopram/paroxetine) sit at Tier 3 or Tier 4. Sertraline 50 mg tablet was picked as the single preferred agent to match this app's convention (see ny-medicaid-ssris) since the document itself does not single out one SSRI over the others -- all four Tier-1 generics are equally 'preferred' by tier placement. The paRequired brand-name entries (Zoloft, Prozac, Celexa, Lexapro, Paxil, Luvox) are an inference, not an explicit non-formulary listing: full-text search of all 108 PDF pages confirmed none of those six brand names appear anywhere in the document, and this Humana guide is framed as an exhaustive 'list of covered drugs' (page 10), so absence from that list means the brand is not covered absent a formulary exception -- standard for a Part D plan once an AB-rated generic exists. No class-wide step-therapy criterion for SSRIs was found anywhere in the document. [Reused: same national Humana Premier Rx PDP formulary as the TX guide (2026-10-21)]
